oa-goldman-sachs-13.title: Find Last Kid
oa-goldman-sachs-13.upstreamSnapshot: The statement truncates at 'random numbe…'; sample N=5,T=2,D=1 expects 2. The accompanying explanation and all three reference implementations treat D as a per-delivery step, which yields 3 for that sample.
oa-goldman-sachs-13.corroboratingSourceText: The full FastPrep page says D is the random number where distribution starts, and children sit in ascending circular order; it repeats the same sample and output 2.
oa-goldman-sachs-13.reason: FastPrep's statement favors D as a starting position, but the immutable OAMaster explanation and Python/Java/C++ implementations use D as the step size. The sole shared sample does not distinguish all possible interpretations; moreover the bundled reference and expected sample directly disagree. Do not promote a judge specification until an authoritative rule resolves the conflict.
